reviewer_identity: storyboard-critic / claude-opus-5-5 high, isolated, read-only exact-phone review

subject_recognition.observed: At 270 px wide each principal object can be named without the board. Anonymous forearms type at a keyboard. A clipboard chart has teal tabs and a clip. The labelled teal 'OpenEvidence AI tool' box has a slot underneath. An 'Answer' card has a 'Sources' slot of three colored chips and a dashed 'Accuracy' box with an empty ring. Three citation cards read 'Medical literature', 'Clinical guidelines' and 'Other sources' (18-21 s). A 12-tile board of faceless clinician silhouettes in coats and scrubs sits over a 'Half / More than half' bar (22-28 s). Large tags read 'Accuracy / Not in release' and 'Patient care / Not in release' (31-32 s). No face and no identifiable clinician appears anywhere. The weak spot is 16.0-17.0 s: about 90 percent of the frame is empty beige floor, and the answer card is only about 75 px wide. At 17 s the three citation cards appear at small size, with their labels too small to read until 18 s.

contact_and_consequence.observed: At 0 s fingertips rest on the keys and the 'Question' card sits on the chart. At 1 s the card is gone from the chart, and at 3-4 s the Answer card rests below the tool with three chips in Sources. That is a readable before and after, though the card's flight isn't visible at one frame per second. At 11-13 s the masked credential field goes from 5 to 8 dots under fingers on the keys. At 14-15 s 'Question' fills with word bars and a 'Plain language' pill under one hand on the keys. At 7 s and 9 s the date tags hang from drawn pins on the teal record boundary. Every card and tag has a drop shadow onto the surface it rests on. The stills don't show the record lock opening (13 s) or the card sliding to the chart edge (15 s), and no hand touches a card. The send reads as a diagram transfer triggered at the keyboard.

dominant_action.observed: In each case the change happens to the focal object itself. At 22-23 s the clinician tiles light from 2 to about 7 of 12 and the bar fills past the Half tick to 'More than half'. At 25 s the 'Clinical decision support' tag appears on the bar, and at 28 s the 'UTMB's own report' tag hangs from the bar's end pin. At 30 s two tags are clipped to the answer, and at 31-32 s they fill the frame reading 'Not in release'. At 34-35 s the 'Medical literature' card descends with a thread into the Sources slot. At 36-38 s the dashed Accuracy ring stays empty, and at 37 s it is visibly brighter. A labelled box or camera drift never stands in for a missing change. One weakness is 19-21 s: three nearly identical frames, so the two 'lift' events show little change at this sampling, and the section reads as an evidence hold with readable tabs.

surface_finish.observed: The style is a consistent flat editorial illustration. Paper cards have soft drop shadows, the chart paper is ruled, and the clipboard has a steel clip and lopsided teal tabs. The tags have pin heads and strings, and a laminate floor with plank lines sits under a window with a grassy plain and a broad flat-topped tree. The weakest surfaces are the hands: flat brown fill, little knuckle or nail detail, sausage-like fingers and long forearms leaving the bottom edge (0-1, 11-15 s). The OpenEvidence tool is a plain bevelled teal box. These are flaws in polish, not unfinished placeholders. Three small defects: at 31-32 s and at the close a tag string runs diagonally across the Accuracy tag's lettering; at 36-38 s the thread crosses the word 'Answer'; and the 'native' stills supplied are 270x480, so no native-crop finish inspection was possible.

continuity.observed: The same chart, tool, answer card, citation set and clinician board carry through every cut, and the disclosure pill stays on screen throughout. Two continuity cheats are visible. In s8, at 39-41 s, the decision and report tags are no longer on the bar, and the 'Evaluating use and experience' tag hangs from the end pin where 'UTMB's own report' hung at 28 s. A viewer may read the attribution as replaced, though the bar and figures are conserved. At the 41.75 s cut the clinician figures leave and only the bar strip remains along the top edge, with the disclosure pill just under it.

closing_payoff.observed: At 41 s the bar reads 'Half | More than half' and the 'Evaluating use and experience' tag hangs from its end pin. Below it the OpenEvidence box is cut to 'penEvidence / tool' at the left edge, under the caption plate. From 42 s to 43 s the frame holds an identical closing picture, with nothing changing between the two sampled seconds. The bar and evaluating tag run along the top, the clipboard chart stands at left, about 30 percent cropped, and the Answer card shows filled Sources chips, an empty dashed Accuracy ring and both 'Accuracy / Not in release' and 'Patient care / Not in release' tags. It answers 'what comes back' (sources) and shows the limit (accuracy and care not published, evaluation continuing) without inventing an outcome. It is a recap of the 31-38 s images at smaller scale rather than a new image, and its 'Not in release' lettering is about 9 px tall, readable but small.

first_frame.observed: Frame 0 is a populated clinic wide with no title card: two forearms on a keyboard, a chart with a small 'Question' card, the teal OpenEvidence box and the clinician board. By 1 s the question card has left the chart, a visible change inside 1.5 s. The card is small, about 50 px at phone width, so the first change is easy to miss next to the large hands.

visual_progression.observed: The states build on each other. A question goes in (0-1). An answer with three source chips comes back (3-4). Date tags pin to the record (7, 9). Credentials fill and a plain-language question is typed (11-15). Citation cards are named (17-21). The clinician share passes half (22-23) and is tagged as decision support (25) and as UTMB's own report (28). Limit tags read Not in release (30-32). The citation thread is traced and the Accuracy ring stays empty (34-38). The evaluation tag lands (39-40). Each shot adds a new state, not a rescan of the same tableau.

shot_variety.observed: The film uses at least four framings. There are room wides (0-1, 5-7), a close on the tool (2-4), tag closes (8-10), a keyboard detail (11-15), a high wide over the floor (16-17), a medium on the citation fan (18-21), a close on the clinician board (22-23), a tilted medium (24-26), a large tag close (31-32), a small wide (33-35), an Accuracy-slot detail (36-38) and the closing composite (42-43). The weakness is that 16-21 and 29-38 share the same beige floor and card idiom.

performed_turn.observed: At 30 s the 'Accuracy' and 'Patient care' tags appear clipped to the returned answer's own clip. At 31-32 s they fill the frame reading 'Not in release'. At 34-35 s the literature thread reaches the Sources slot, while at 36-38 s the dashed Accuracy ring stays empty and brightens at 37 s. The turn from 'sources came back' to 'nothing shows it is right' is drawn on the same answer card.

pace.observed: New visible information arrives at about 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 14, 17, 18, 22, 23, 25, 28, 30, 31, 34, 36, 37 and 39 s, so no observed gap exceeds 4 s. The slowest stretches are 19-21 s (near-identical frames, read as an evidence hold on readable tabs) and 41.75-44 s (identical 42 and 43 s frames, a closing hold).

closing_answer.observed: The last image holds the answer with filled Sources and an empty Accuracy ring, both Not in release tags, the chart, and the evaluating tag on the More-than-half bar. It answers what comes back and what isn't published, and it invents no outcome. It recaps the turn's imagery rather than adding a new picture. The bar's 'Half | More than half' labels sit within about 8 px of the top edge under the disclosure pill, which reads close to a crop.

finished_art.observed: The art is coherent and deliberate at phone size: soft shadows, paper and teal card stock, copper reserved for the limit tags, worn clipboard edges and readable type. It looks finished for its flat editorial style and isn't decorative filler. The hands are the least finished element (flat fill, tubular fingers, long forearms). Native-scale finish is unverified because the supplied 'native' stills are phone-sized.

About 90 percent of the frame is empty beige floor around a roughly 75 px Answer card, and the citation cards arrive only at 17 s at unreadable label size. The close at 41.75-44.0 s is next weakest: a static recap, two identical sampled frames, the clipboard about 30 percent cropped, the bar labels near the top edge under the disclosure pill, and a tag string across the Accuracy tag. Non-blocking notes: (1) at 39-41 s the decision and report tags are gone from the bar without being moved on screen, and the evaluating tag takes the report tag's end pin; (2) the 'penEvidence' crop under the caption at 39.5-41.75 s; (3) the string crossing the Accuracy tag's lettering at 31-32 s and the close; (4) the thread crossing 'Answer' at 36-38 s; (5) the hands are the least finished art; (6) the window plain with a flat-topped tree reads as generic grassland. It isn't contradictory to the Gulf Coast, but at 270 px it isn't clearly coastal either.
limits: This review used only the supplied stills: four contact sheets per film at one frame per second (270x480) and two 'native' stills per film at 41 and 42.9 s, which are also 270x480. Motion between frames, card and hand trajectories, the lock opening, the glow and pulse timing, any velocity or stutter faults, and the transient positions inside 1-second gaps can't be seen. The card send at about 0.6-1.5 s, the slide to the chart edge at about 15 s, the citation lifts at 18-21 s and the evaluating-tag settle at 39.9-41 s are judged only from their before and after states. Native-crop surface finish wasn't inspectable. No sound or audio sync was reviewed, and sound remains owed to the audiovisual lenses. Caption timings are authored estimates from the board, not measured. SHA256 values are echoed from the output contract; a Read-only reviewer can't recompute them. This verdict is a muted phone preflight on these bytes only. It approves no score, narration take or shipment, and the timed measured phone, native hero, audiovisual and panel reviews still apply.
